Press Down for answers

Answer 1

What is the time complexity of binary search?

O(log n) — logarithmic time.

Answer 2

Does binary search work on unsorted data?

No — data must be sorted first.

Answer 3

What does a recursive function need to avoid infinite loops?

A base case that stops the recursion.

The Big Question

🤔 You build a game with a high score system.

You close the program... where did the scores go?

❌ Problem: RAM is volatile.

Variables only exist while the program runs. Power off = data gone.

✅ Solution: Persistence via files.

Save data to secondary storage (HDD/SSD) — it survives program termination.

File Modes

When opening a file, you must specify what you want to do with it.

Mode Description Concept
'r' Read mode. Default. Opens for reading. Error if file doesn't exist. Look only
'w' Write mode. Creates new file or overwrites existing one. New / Rewrite
'a' Append mode. Adds data to the end of the file. Add on

Reading data

The safest way to open files in Python is using the with statement, which automatically closes the file even if errors occur.

# Reading a text file
with open("names.txt", "r") as file:
    # Read all lines into a list
    lines = file.readlines()

for line in lines:
    print(line.strip())  # strip() removes newline \n

.strip() is crucial because lines often end with invisible \n characters.

Writing data

names = ["Alice", "Bob", "Charlie"]

# 'w' mode overwrites the file
with open("names.txt", "w") as file:
    for name in names:
        file.write(name + "\n")  # Add newline manually!

Important Notes

  • write() only accepts strings. You must cast numbers: str(score).
  • write() does not add a new line automatically. You must add + "\n".

Parallel Arrays

Using multiple lists to store related data, linked by their index.

IndexNAMESSCORES
0Annabelle50
1Benjamin35
2Claire70
names = ["Annabelle", "Benjamin", "Claire"]
scores = [50, 35, 70]

# Accessing related data
i = 2
print(f"{names[i]} scored {scores[i]}")
# Claire scored 70

Scenario: Loading Sales Data

Convert sales.txt into parallel arrays.

File: sales.txt

Amina,23424
Carlos,42549
Emily,52488
names = []
sales = []

with open("sales.txt", "r") as file:
    for line in file:
        # Split line by comma
        parts = line.strip().split(",")
        names.append(parts[0])
        sales.append(int(parts[1]))

print(names) # ['Amina', 'Carlos', 'Emily']
print(sales) # [23424, 42549, 52488]

Scenario: Saving Leaderboard

Save user scores to a formatted text file.

leader_name = ["Annabelle", "Benjamin"]
leader_points = [19, 21]

with open("leaderboard.txt", "w") as file:
    for i in range(len(leader_name)):
        # Construct the line string
        entry = f"{leader_name[i]}: {leader_points[i]}\n"
        file.write(entry)

# leaderboard.txt content:
# Annabelle: 19
# Benjamin: 21

Code Challenge

Task: Create a persistent high score system.

  1. Ask the user for their name and score.
  2. Append this data to a file scores.txt.
  3. Then, read the file and print all previous high scores.

Press Down for Solution

Solution

# 1. Get Input
name = input("Enter name: ")
score = input("Enter score: ")

# 2. Append to file
with open("scores.txt", "a") as f:
    f.write(f"{name},{score}\n")

# 3. Read and Display
print("\n--- HIGH SCORES ---")
with open("scores.txt", "r") as f:
    for line in f:
        data = line.strip().split(",")
        print(f"{data[0]}: {data[1]}")

🧠 Quick Check

State the three file modes and their purpose.

'r' = Read, 'w' = Write (overwrites), 'a' = Append (adds to end).

Misconception Check

A. 'w' mode appends data to the end of a file.

B. Opening a non-existent file in 'r' mode causes an error.

C. .write() automatically adds newlines.

D. The with statement auto-closes the file.

Press Down for answers

Answers

A: False. 'w' overwrites; 'a' appends.

B: True. You get a FileNotFoundError.

C: False. You must manually add \n.

D: True. with handles closing automatically.

Key Takeaways

  • Persistence — files store data beyond program execution.
  • File modes: 'r' (read), 'w' (write/overwrite), 'a' (append).
  • Use with open() for automatic file closing.
  • .strip() removes trailing newlines; .split() parses CSV data.
  • Parallel arrays link related data by index position.

End of B2: You've covered programming fundamentals → algorithms → file I/O!
